content: For hematogenous osteomyelitis in adults over the age of 21, if methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is suspected, the preferred treatment is vancomycin administered intravenously at a dose of 1 gram every 12 hours. For patients weighing over 100 kilograms, the dose should be increased to 1.5 grams intravenously every 12 hours. If MRSA is not suspected, the preferred treatment is nafcillin or oxacillin, each given at a dose of 2 grams intravenously every 4 hours. For children older than 4 months with suspected MRSA, the recommended treatment is vancomycin at a dose of 40 milligrams per kilogram per day, administered intravenously every 6 to 8 hours. If MRSA is unlikely, nafcillin or oxacillin is preferred, dosed at 37 milligrams per kilogram intravenously every 6 hours, with a maximum daily dose of 8 to 12 grams. If Gram-negative bacilli are identified on Gram stain, ceftazidime (50 milligrams per kilogram intravenously every 8 hours) or cefepime (150 milligrams per kilogram per day intravenously every 8 hours) should be added. For pathogen-directed therapy in cases of methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA), the preferred regimens include nafcillin or oxacillin at 2 grams intravenously every 4 hours, or cefazolin at 2 grams intravenously every 8 hours. Vancomycin (1 gram intravenously every 12 hours, or 1.5 grams for patients over 100 kilograms) is an alternative. For MRSA, vancomycin remains the preferred treatment, while linezolid (600 milligrams intravenously or orally every 12 hours) with or without rifampin (300 milligrams orally or intravenously twice daily) is an alternative. For contiguous osteomyelitis with vascular insufficiency, it is essential to debride the overlying ulcer and obtain a bone specimen for histological and microbiological analysis. Empiric antimicrobial therapy is not recommended unless the patient is acutely ill. Antibiotic therapy should be guided by culture results, and treatment should last for at least 6 weeks. Revascularization should be performed if feasible. In cases of open fracture osteomyelitis involving long bones after internal fixation, if Staphylococcus aureus or Pseudomonas aeruginosa is suspected, the preferred regimen is vancomycin (1 gram intravenously every 12 hours) combined with either ceftazidime (2 grams intravenously every 8 hours) or cefepime (2 grams intravenously every 8 hours). Alternative regimens include linezolid (600 milligrams intravenously or orally twice daily) combined with either ceftazidime or cefepime at the same doses. For infections caused by Gram-negative bacilli, ciprofloxacin (750 milligrams orally twice daily) or levofloxacin (750 milligrams orally once daily) is preferred. For diabetic foot osteomyelitis, in cases of chronic infection or recent antibiotic use, several preferred regimens are available, including levofloxacin (750 milligrams intravenously or orally every 24 hours), cefoxitin (1 gram intravenously every 4 hours or 2 grams intravenously every 6 to 8 hours), ceftriaxone (1 to 2 grams intravenously or intramuscularly every 12 to 24 hours), ampicillin-sulbactam (1.5 to 3 grams intravenously or intramuscularly every 6 hours), moxifloxacin (400 milligrams intravenously or orally every 24 hours), ertapenem (1 gram intravenously or intramuscularly every 24 hours), tigecycline (100 milligrams intravenously as a loading dose, followed by 50 milligrams intravenously every 12 hours), or imipenem-cilastatin (0.5 to 1 gram intravenously every 6 to 8 hours). Alternative regimens include combinations of levofloxacin or ciprofloxacin with clindamycin, with dosing adjusted based on severity. For patients at high risk of MRSA, the preferred regimens include linezolid (600 milligrams intravenously or orally every 12 hours), daptomycin (4 milligrams per kilogram intravenously every 24 hours), or vancomycin (15 to 20 milligrams per kilogram intravenously every 8 to 12 hours, with a target trough level of 10 to 20 milligrams per liter). For those at high risk of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, piperacillin-tazobactam (3.375 grams intravenously every 6 to 8 hours) is recommended. For polymicrobial infections, the preferred regimen includes a combination of vancomycin, linezolid, or daptomycin with piperacillin-tazobactam, imipenem-cilastatin, ertapenem, or meropenem. An alternative regimen involves combining vancomycin, linezolid, or daptomycin with ceftazidime, cefepime, or aztreonam, along with metronidazole.
